title: Taiwan reportedly indicted NVIDIA employees for exporting prohibited AI servers to China
content:
Taiwan reportedly indicted NVIDIA employees for exporting prohibited AI servers to China
The nine individuals are accused of 'severely damaged our nation's image,' prosecutors said.
Although the US has relaxed its restrictions on NVIDIA AI chip exports to China, illegal exports apparently still take place. Prosecutors in Taiwan just indicted nine individuals, including NVIDIA and Super Micro employees, for illegally bringing AI servers into China, Reuters reported.
The defendants "colluded with one another at various levels for enormous profit, illegally exporting high-end servers, increasing corporate compliance costs, and severely damaging our nation's international image," prosecutors from the northern city of Keelung said in a statement. They did this, the team added, despite being "fully aware" of NVIDIA and Super Micro's "rigorous" export control procedures.
Although NVIDIA is an American company, most of its chips are manufactured by the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world's largest chip maker by far. TSMC's latest Blackwell AI chips are manufactured in Phoenix, Arizona, but are still shipped to Taiwan for advanced packaging prior to final assembly.
The US has banned the sale of cutting-edge AI tech from NVIDIA and others to China since 2022. Recently, it has allowed sales to China of previous-generation products like H200 chips that are several years old. Taiwan is ultra-strict about exports of newer technology, lest it displease US regulators and, in particular, the Trump administration.
Despite Taiwan's clampdown, bad actors have found ways to get such chips into China. In one instance, $1 billion worth of server racks may have been shipped through Southeast Asian countries like Thailand or Malaysia to circumvent US export controls. In another case, the US charged three people with allegedly exporting $3.5 billion worth of AI servers to China, again by routing them through third-party countries.

report.summary: 台湾起诉NVIDIA等员工非法出口AI服务器至中国。
report.background: 美国自2022年起禁止英伟达等向中国出口尖端AI芯片，近期仅允许H200等旧款。台湾为避免得罪美国，对新技术出口极为严格。但非法出口仍通过泰国、马来西亚等第三国转运，此前有案例涉及35亿美元。此次基隆检方起诉显示台方加大执法。
key_points: 台湾基隆检方起诉九人，包括NVIDIA和超微员工，指控其合谋非法出口高端AI服务器至中国。
被告明知公司有严格出口管制程序，仍为巨额利润违法，检方称严重损害台湾国际形象。
美国2022年起限制尖端AI芯片对华出口，近期仅放开H200等旧款，但非法转运渠道仍在运作。
非法出口多经东南亚第三国规避管制，此前曾有案件涉及35亿美元，此次起诉凸显执法收紧。
report.impact: 对AI行业：暴露出口管制执行漏洞，可能导致美中技术封锁升级，供应链承压。对开发者：国际合作面临更多合规审查，AI研发所用硬件获取受限。对普通用户：非法芯片流动减少可能影响终端产品价格与供应，但长期利于规范市场。
report.tools: 可关注美国商务部BIS出口管制清单更新及英伟达官方合规说明；暂无特定开源工具，可参考OpenSanctions数据用于尽职调查。
